findings.evidence: Design and review SQL and MongoDB schemas - tables or collections, keys, foreign keys, constraints, multi-tenant isolation, soft deletes, timestamp and money types, query-aligned indexes, and staged live migrations (expand-contract, NOT NULL, online DDL) for PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite.
findings.fix: Design and review SQL and MongoDB schemas: tables or collections, keys, foreign keys, constraints, multi-tenant isolation, soft deletes, timestamp and money types, query-aligned indexes, and staged live migrations (expand-contract, NOT NULL, online DDL) for PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite. Use when someone needs a data model, DDL, an ERD-ready table list, an embed-or-reference decision, a schema review, or a safe migration plan, even if they only describe entities and queries or a symptom such as re-signup failing after a soft delete, cross-tenant data leaking, or a migration that locked production. Not for REST or GraphQL API models, ORM classes for an existing schema, data-warehouse dashboards, database deployment, backups or connection pooling, or tuning a query without changing the schema.

findings.evidence: In MongoDB, embed a child only when it is read with its parent, bounded in size, owned by that parent alone, and updated atomically with it. Reference it when it is shared across parents, grows without bound (see the 16 MiB gotcha), is queried on its own, or is updated independently at a high rate.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: when the criteria conflict (read with the parent, but shared or unbounded), reference it and keep at most the bounded slice from the 16 MiB gotcha.
